title: First conditional
note: If/when + present, will + base. Real future. Light zero. Gap on will/won't or present verb. · Bank 48 items · flags: 2026-07-26f vocab+accepts · sequencing rewrite 2026-08-06 (cloud): 29/48 items re-lexified onto pool-legal words; 'rain' kept as the single logged fork · intro rewritten student-facing 2026-08-16 (was authoring shorthand — James, smoking for Patrik) · gap-half rewrite 2026-08-19 (James, Patrik smoke): 17 blanks moved onto the if/time clause — the bank only ever tested the result half; + 6 as soon as/until/after items the intro promised · 2026-08-20 (James, smoke): "this is zero conditional and it is labelled first conditional — sloppy, embarrassing". cards.title: First conditional
cards.body: A real possibility in the future: if this happens, that will happen. The if-part uses the present simple; the result uses will + verb.
cards.body_cz: Reálná možnost v budoucnosti: když se stane tohle, stane se tamto. Část s if používá přítomný čas prostý; výsledek používá will + sloveso.
points: The if-part uses the PRESENT — even though the meaning is future.
Never **will** in the if-part: ~~If it **will** rain~~.
The order can flip: I **will** stay home if it **rains**.

cards.title: Examples

table.caption: English ↔ Czech
rows: Když se budeš učit, uděláš to.

points: Czech uses the FUTURE in both halves (když bude pršet). English keeps the if-part in the present — that is the trap.
when, until and as soon as work like if: When I **finish**, I **will** call you.

cards.title: Negatives
cards.body: Negative in the if-part: don't / doesn't. Negative result: won't.
cards.body_cz: Zápor v části s if: don't / doesn't. Záporný výsledek: won't.

table.caption: examples
rows: If it **doesn't** rain, we **will** go out.
If you **don't** hurry, you **will** miss the train.

cards.title: Questions
cards.body: In the question, will moves before the person. The if-part does not change.
cards.body_cz: V otázce se will přesune před osobu. Část s if se nemění.

table.caption: examples
rows: If you **miss** the bus, how **will** you get home?

points: **will** + person in the question half: What **will** you do…?

cards.title: Zero conditional — facts (a different one)
cards.body: This is NOT the first conditional. It has its own name: the **zero conditional**. Use it when something is ALWAYS true — a fact, not a future plan. Both halves use the present, and there is no **will** anywhere.
cards.body_cz: Tohle NENÍ první kondicionál. Má vlastní název: **nultý kondicionál**. Používá se, když něco platí VŽDY — fakt, ne budoucí plán. Obě části jsou v přítomném čase a **will** tam není vůbec.

table.caption: facts
rows: If you **don't** water plants, they die.

points: Zero conditional (always true): If you heat ice, it **melts**.
First conditional (one future possibility): If it **rains**, I **will** stay home.
The difference is **will** — a fact never has it.
Nultý = vždy platí. První = jedna budoucí možnost. Rozdíl je **will**.

cards.title: Remember
points: If + present, **will** + verb: If it **rains**, I **will** stay home.
when / until / as soon as work like if: When I **finish**, I **will** call you.
